name: Craig Isaf hut, solo weekend
summary: A stone hut for one practitioner to run their own weekend of long sitting. No teacher. Silence except for the evening exchange when supper arrives. £40.
description:
Craig Isaf is a two-room hut at 400 metres that a small sangha has kept since the eighties. There is no teacher and no programme. We lend it to one person at a time who already sits and wants a weekend of sitting a lot, alone, without anyone organising them.

You arrange the weekend yourself. Most people settle on a rhythm on Friday night: five or six sits a day of forty-five minutes to an hour, walking between, starting early. Some sit longer. The hut has a cushion, a bench, a stove, and a bell. What you do with them is yours.

Silence is kept from waking until the evening meal. Supper is the exception: Pauline brings it up from the farm at six and stays for a cup of tea, and most people find that half hour of ordinary talk is where the day gets digested. After she goes, silence again.

It is a demanding way to spend two days. The sitting is long, the hut is cold in the mornings, the hill is steep, and there is nobody to tell you to ease off. We ask that you have an established daily practice and have done at least one residential retreat. We do not check, but the hut is not a good place to find out you were not ready.

Pauline holds the key and lives in the farm below. Apart from supper she leaves you alone.
practical: Friday evening to Sunday afternoon, most weekends. £40 for the weekend, to the sangha, covering wood, upkeep, and the two suppers. Sleeps one on a platform; bring a bag and a mat. Cold water, wood stove, composting toilet, no electricity. Bring breakfast and lunch food; the nearest shop is nine miles. Park at the farm and walk twenty minutes up. No signal at the hut.
